thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High-rate GPU OOMs detected in streaming pool `g4-decode-pool` across nodes g4-12-*/g4-15-*. Multiple CUDA OOM and container restarts observed. Automatic circuit-breaker did not trigger (threshold mismatch). Paging oncall.

sara: acknowledging, hopping on. which customer(s) impacted? :wave:

kyle: seeing repeated logs like `CUDA_OUT_OF_MEMORY: std::bad_alloc` during decode streams, spike started ~00:05 UTC. Kernel logs show `invalid device pointer` on one host before restart.

matt: confirmed request drops. Explorer shows 3% 5xx for streaming traffic in the last 2m and a handful of client retries. No high CPU on control plane.

anjali: tagging CS — @josh-cs can you correlate tickets? worried about regen / double-charge issues.

josh-cs: I have two customer reports (TCK-8891, TCK-8892) complaining partial responses + immediate retries. Not yet escalated. I'll mark severity=high and notify account teams.

sara: immediate mitigation plan:
1) flip circuit-breaker to strict for streaming on path `/v1/generate/stream` (lower threshold)
2) enforce `x-client-max-tokens: 512` at ingress for suspect clients
3) failover to `redwood-small-1` for bursty clients
4) rolling restart of affected decode pods with `--clear-kv-cache`

kyle: implementing 1 & 2 now. pushing policy change to envoy with a short-lived route override.

ops-bot: Envoy route patch applied: `route_override/streaming-burst-throttle` -> enabled

kyle: applying header injection rule:

```
# envoy admin config snippet
route_match: { prefix: "/v1/generate/stream" }
request_headers_to_add:
  - header: { key: "x-client-max-tokens", value: "512" }
```

matt: also adding per-client token-socket limit to slow down regen storms. Will drop requests exceeding 10 concurrent streams per API key.

anjali: patching fallback routing: any 429/5xx on `g4-decode` now returns 200 proxied response from `redwood-small-1` with a `x-fallback-model` header.

sara: rolling restart command for one node group (doing canary 2/10):

```
kubectl rollout restart statefulset/g4-decode --namespace=prod --selector=pool=g4-decode-pool --grace-period=30
kubectl exec -it pod/g4-decode-12 -- /bin/sh -c "rm -rf /tmp/kv-cache && supervisorctl restart decode-worker"
```

incident-bot: Pager duty: `oncall` notified. Current priority: P1. Incident channel created.

kyle: noticed large KV cache growth before OOMs — some clients sending long prefixes. Evicting oldest 20% entries on the canary pods.

matt: post-canary, pod g4-decode-12 restarted cleanly and served steady for 3m. No new OOM logs on that pod.

sara: escalating to infra: possible memory leak in recent decode runtime (release 2026.02.11). @eng-sre please triage with a memory profiler capture.

eng-sre (matt): started heap traces on two affected hosts. uploading snapshot to S3: s3://redwood-ops/oom-dumps/5067890123/

anjali: customer-facing note draft: "We've observed streaming request drops due to GPU memory exhaustion in our decode cluster. We've throttled bursty clients, enabled a temporary token cap, and routed requests to a lower-capacity fallback model. We're investigating root cause and will provide a post-incident summary." Will paste to CS.

josh-cs: I've sent the note to the two affected customers, offered regen credits and a short workaround (use non-streaming endpoint or pin to Dedicated). Awaiting responses.

kyle: after canary success, started rolling restart of remaining pods (8/10). Applied eviction and KV cache clear during restart. Monitoring.

ops-bot: Alert suppression enabled for duplicated OOMs to reduce noise. New alerts will require unique stack traces.

matt: small spike at 00:28 UTC on one remaining node; restarted that pod manually, cleared `/dev/shm` and resized shared mem to avoid transient allocation failures.

sara: status update to broader channel: short partial customer impact (estimated ~280 requests dropped across 18 customers), mitigations applied (token cap, fallback routing, KV eviction, rolling restarts). Root-cause investigation ongoing. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Summary log excerpt:
```
[00:05:12] decode-worker[pid=3245] ERROR CUDA_OUT_OF_MEMORY: allocation 215MB failed on device 0
[00:05:13] supervisor restarting decode-worker (exit_code=137)
[00:05:15] kernel: watchdog: reset invoked for container g4-decode-12
```

anjali: follow-ups:
- revert the temporary route override after 2h if stable
- open rollback PR for recent runtime change if mem profiler shows leak in 2026.02.11
- add an automatic circuit-breaker tied to KV cache growth metric
- run a backfill eval on long-prefix clients to measure cost

sara: handing off to night oncall @kyle (oncall Handoff). I'll create the incident postmortem draft and include timeline + customer impact. Leaving channel open for updates.

kyle: taking handoff. Notes copied to incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-5067. I'll keep watch for any regressions and coordinate with eng-sre tomorrow for heap analysis.

josh-cs: customers acknowledged workaround, one asked for Dedicated migration steps. I'll coordinate with account team.

sara: great work team. final state at handoff: cluster stable, OOM rate back to baseline, customer impact contained. Postmortem owner assigned: anjali. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P1 moved to monitoring. Incident channel will remain open for 4h for observation.
